known.title: docs/PLAN-QUEUE.md adds a live file:line anchor, but docs/AGENTS.md allows file:line anchors only in point-in-time records.
known.summary: The diff adds this sentence to docs/PLAN-QUEUE.md:9: 'An empty `Depends on` cell is `-`; `parseQueue` reads it as no dependency (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:973).' The anchor plan.mjs:973 names a real line of a real file in the repository. docs/AGENTS.md is the nearest AGENTS.md of docs/PLAN-QUEUE.md. docs/AGENTS.md:21-25 names the point-in-time records: docs/release-evidence/, docs/authoring-audits.md, and docs/optimization-audit-may-2026.md. docs/AGENTS.md:27-29 says: '`file:line` anchors are allowed only in those point-in-time records. Long-lived documentation and context-tree nodes must use the durable grammar: `` `path` — `symbol/config key` — purpose (verify: `command`) ``.' docs/PLAN-QUEUE.md is not a point-in-time record. docs/AGENTS.md:14 calls it the optional discovery and priority view, and it stays live. The anchor rots on the next edit above that line. Example: this same PR moves the parseQueue sentinel line from 965 at the base commit to 973 at head, so the same sentence written at the base would now point at the wrong line. No CI guard catches it, because scripts/skills/durable-anchors.mjs scans only skill files and AGENTS.md nodes. Fix: remove the anchor, or use the durable grammar with the path, the `parseQueue` symbol, and a purpose.

known.title: The em-dash refusal is a new check 14, so the plan-manager skill text that says check and edit run 13 checks is now wrong.
known.summary: checkPlan pushes 'check 14: body contains an em dash' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:278). This is a new fourteenth check number after 'check 13' (plan.mjs:277). The test regex at scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:568 also changes to /check 14: body contains an em dash/. The command table of plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/SKILL.md, which the diff does not change, still says '`edit` runs 13 checks' (SKILL.md:228) and '`check <issue | --file <path>>` | 13 checks' (SKILL.md:229). The plan-cli summary line at scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:2383 still prints 'plan CLI contract: 13 checks'. The plan says the refusal 'is in the check 10 family with its own message, so the pinned "13 checks" count does not change' (Research), and the Done-when cell of step body_dash_ban says 'the "13 checks" count does not change'. Scenario: `plan.mjs check --file <body>` on a body with an em dash prints 'check 14: body contains an em dash', but the skill tells the agent that check runs 13 checks, so the agent finds no rule 14. Fix: emit the refusal as a check 10 message next to the machine-path check, and keep the test regex on check 10.

known.title: The em-dash check scans the body after it blanks fenced code blocks, so a plan body with an em dash inside a code fence passes check and edit.
known.summary: The refusal at plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:278 tests blankFencedRegions(planText).includes('\u2014'). blankFencedRegions (plan.mjs:93-105) replaces every character of each line inside a ``` or ~~~ fence, the fence lines included, with a space. So the check does not see an em dash inside a fenced block. The contract says 'A plan body contains no U+2014 em dash character anywhere.' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:104; the same sentence is in docs/PLAN.md:91 and plan-md-template.md:95). The plan says '`checkPlan` gets an em-dash refusal for the whole body' and step body_dash_ban says 'Refuse any em dash in a plan body'. Checked with Node v24.22.1: a valid v3 body whose `## Research` holds the three lines '```text', '### Plan review — 2026-08-08', '```' gives checkPlan(...) = [] with this code, but ['check 10: body contains an em dash'] with a whole-body test. Thus `check`, `edit` (plan.mjs editPlan calls checkPlan before the write), and the mutators that call requireValidPlanIssue accept and keep a body with an em dash, for example a Research note that quotes an old review heading. The test at scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:563-569 puts the em dash only outside a fence, so it does not cover this. Fix: test the raw planText.
